topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence
target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of Newtonian mechanics and momentum.

sections.title: Introduction: The Paradox of Pi
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless track.
Impacts count digits of the constant pi.
Heavy block mass creates the sequence.
animations: Create two rectangles on a track, #FFFFFF color, labeled 'm1' and 'm2'.
Show M1 moving toward M2 and the wall, labeled #FF0000.
Display the count of collisions as a running number, color #FFFF00.
Transition visual into a circular representation of pi, color #FF00FF.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Conservation of momentum governs the system.
Kinetic energy remains constant during collisions.
animations: Animate two balls colliding, showing velocity vectors with #00FFFF arrows.
Visualize energy conserved, show 'KE1 + KE2 = const' in #FFFF00.
Draw elastic collision path, showing angle reflection with #FF00FF.

sections.title: Mapping Collisions to Phase Space
animations: Draw a 2D plane with X and Y axes, color #808080.
Represent collision as a point hitting a boundary line, color #00FF00.
Show the geometric path reflecting in the phase space, color #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Limit of Infinity (100^n)
lecture_lines: Mass ratio impacts grow with magnitude.
Number of collisions converges to pi.
animations: Show collision count converging toward pi, color #FFFF00.
Visual transition from blocks to a circle arc, color #00FFFF.
Increase number of digits displayed, color #00FF00.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuitive Synthesis
lecture_lines: Physics acts as an analog computer.
animations: Show digital computer simulation of colliding blocks, color #00FF00.
Display rotating circular symmetry overlaying the collision, color #FF00FF.
Final overlay of pi emerging from the movement, color #FFFFFF.
